name: Kosovo
summary: Kosovo had 1,457 battery-electric passenger cars at the end of 2025 (Eurostat), 51% more than a year earlier, and 539 new ones were registered that year. Imports are rising: 780 electric cars came in during January–August 2026, 665 of them from China. Electric cars get no tax break — they pay the same import taxes as petrol and diesel cars: 10% customs duty, 18% VAT and, on used cars, excise by age. ECHARGE is the only network that publishes prices: €0.39–0.49 per kWh on DC and €0.21 (day) / €0.19 (night) on AC, without saying whether VAT is included. At home, night-rate electricity costs about 4.2 euro cents per kWh with VAT while the household stays within 800 kWh a month.

public_count.note: ECHARGE states '24+' stations and names cities in Kosovo and Albania, without a list; Radio Free Europe (06.04.2026) reported 32 ECHARGE charge points in the Prishtina region, on the Prishtina–Tirana route and in Albania. RapidCharge shows 2 stations in Prishtina and HIB Petrol gives no number. The local-language map on this site showed 21 locations on 28.09.2026, merged from Open Charge Map (17 records) and OpenStreetMap (5 records) and not checked one by one.

electricity.what: Households up to 800 kWh a month, day / night
electricity.price: 9.05 / 3.88 euro cents per kWh without VAT (VAT 8%)
electricity.note: Tariffs from 01.05.2025 (ERO decision V_2703_2025); ERO left retail prices unchanged for 2026. With 8% VAT (calculated): 9.77 / 4.19 cents. The low (night) tariff applies 22:00–07:00 from 1 October to 31 March and 23:00–08:00 from 1 April to 30 September. A fixed monthly charge comes on top (see below).
electricity.source_title: Buletini Ekonomik – ERO approves tariffs without an increase

electricity.what: Households above 800 kWh a month, day / night
electricity.price: 15.43 / 7.28 euro cents per kWh without VAT
electricity.note: Night rate: 7.28 according to Dukagjini (16.04.2025, the day of the decision) and four later reports, consistent with the announced 16.1% rise (checked); only Fikso (16.04.2025) gives 7.21. With 8% VAT (calculated): 16.66 / 7.86 cents. ERO and KESCO do not say whether these prices apply only to the kWh above 800.
electricity.source_title: Dukagjini – ERO formalises the decision: electricity 16.1% dearer from 1 May

electricity.note: Single source: Buletini Ekonomik reports that the April 2025 tariff decision raised it from €2.00 to €2.32. Whether the 8% VAT applies to it is not stated. It is paid with or without an electric car.
electricity.source_title: Buletini Ekonomik – the fixed charge increase

electricity.note: No official fuel price found. Indicative prices of one retailer (Petrol Company, 25.09.2026: diesel €1.94, petrol €1.62) and a media report (Periskopi, 27.09.2026: €1.95 and €1.65); VAT not stated.

subsidies.note: Electric cars pay the same import taxes as petrol and diesel cars: 10% customs duty, 18% VAT and, on used cars, a fixed excise of about €400–700 by age (Gazeta Express, 27.09.2026; Radio Free Europe, 06.04.2026). RTV21 (06.09.2025) reported €400 for an electric car and €10 for a hybrid; the customs tariff itself could not be read, so the exact excise is not confirmed. On 28.08.2024 the Government approved a zero registration tax for electric cars in the draft Law on Vehicles, but in April 2026 Radio Free Europe reported no import or registration relief. The Kosovo Chamber of Commerce has asked to remove the customs duty and cut VAT to 8%; the ministries did not answer the newspaper's questions.
subsidies.source_title: Gazeta Express – China takes the wheel in Kosovo's EV market

subsidies.note: No purchase subsidy and no municipal benefit found (checked 28.09.2026).

buildings.text: The condominium law in force does not mention garages, parking or EV chargers. Ordinary decisions of the owners' association need owners holding more than 50% of the co-ownership (art. 14); works beyond regular administration, including changes to the co-owned parts, need the consent of all owners (art. 32). Which of the two applies to a charger in a shared garage is not stated.
buildings.law: Ligji nr. 03/L-091 për shfrytëzimin, administrimin dhe mirëmbajtjen e ndërtesës në bashkëpronësi, arts. 14, 28 and 32 (adopted 12.03.2009; Official Gazette no. 51, 15.04.2009; no amendment shown)

policy.text: The Energy Strategy 2022–2031, as reviewed, sets no numeric target for electric vehicles or charging stations; Radio Free Europe (06.04.2026) wrote that it foresees about 15,000 electric cars by 2031. The two could not be reconciled.

Prishtina's 2021 e-taxi licensing call requires each licensed operator to install two DC chargers of at least 50 kW, one of them in public space and reported as free for all citizens; whether these chargers exist and are free today was not verified.

gaps: ERO's 2025 tariff decision (V_2703_2025) publishes its tariff table as an image, so household prices come from media; the number of the 2026 decision was not found.
ERO and KESCO do not say whether the above-800 kWh prices apply only to the kWh above 800; the fixed monthly charge (€2.32) comes from a single source.
It is not stated whether ECHARGE prices include VAT, which sites get €0.39 vs €0.49, or which hours count as day and night.

The excise on imported electric cars comes from media only (€400–700 by age for used cars vs €400 per electric car); the customs tariff could not be read. Whether the Assembly passed the zero registration tax for electric cars was not checked.
The share of GB/T connectors among imported Chinese EVs is not documented.
No fast charger on the R6 or R7 motorways was confirmed. The latest source found on motorway tolls (Radio Free Europe, 16.05.2021) says they are toll-free; no 2025–2026 confirmation.
